title: "Resources"

Four places to go deeper than this lesson, or to check a citation yourself before it goes in a
real Lakeshore document. All four were checked and loading at the time this page was written.
Five more entries follow the original four, including the video embedded in this lesson.

- **[21 CFR 820.1, Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/820.1)**
  — the scope section of the QMSR (Quality Management System Regulation), including 820.1(a)(3),
  the paragraph that excludes manufacturers of blood and blood components from Part 820 entirely.
  Read it in full to see the exclusion sitting next to the parallel exclusion for components and
  parts, and the separate inclusion for HCT/Ps (human cells, tissues, and cellular and
  tissue-based products) — three different carve-outs, easy to blur together if you only remember
  one.

- **[21 CFR 820.10, Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/820.10)**
  — the quality-system requirements this lesson quotes from: the top-line "document a QMS
  complying with ISO 13485" requirement, the Class II/III design-and-development requirement, and
  the Part 803/806 complaint and advisory-notice cross-references. Use it to check any ISO 13485
  clause-number citation against the actual CFR text before you repeat it anywhere.

- **[21 CFR 864.9165, eCFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-H/part-864/subpart-J/section-864.9165)**
  — the regulation defining BECS (Blood Establishment Computer Software) and its five special
  controls, including the labeling requirements for unresolved anomalies, revision history, and
  the traceability matrix this lesson treats as vendor deliverables. Module 3 linked Cornell's
  mirror for this same section; eCFR's version is the government's own current, authoritative
  copy, worth bookmarking alongside it.

- **[Federal Register: Medical Devices; Quality System Regulation Amendments](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/02/02/2024-01709/medical-devices-quality-system-regulation-amendments)**
  — the final rule that renamed and restructured Part 820 into the QMSR, published February 2,
  2024, effective February 2, 2026 (document 2024-01709). Use this page to confirm the rule's
  exact title, publication date, and effective date yourself, rather than taking this lesson's
  word for them — and to see the rule's own preamble if you ever need more context than a bare
  citation gives you.

- **[An Overview of the Quality Management System Regulation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Na-OF3OkqEg)**
  (U.S. Food and Drug Administration, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this
  lesson, listed on FDA's CDRH Learn page as a QMSR module. Written for device manufacturers, not
  blood centers, so treat it as the vendor's side of the picture; don't expect it to address
  Lakeshore's position under 820.1(a)(3). Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11
  (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA: Quality Management System Regulation (QMSR)](https://www.fda.gov/medical-devices/postmarket-requirements-devices/quality-management-system-regulation-qmsr)**
  — FDA's own landing page for the QMSR. Read it when someone quotes a QMSR date, scope, or
  FAQ and you want the agency's wording rather than a consultant's summary. Verified loading via
  `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA CDRH Learn](https://www.fda.gov/training-and-continuing-education/cdrh-learn)** — the
  agency's training hub, which lists its QMSR modules, webinars, and town halls with slides and
  transcripts. Useful if you want a transcript to search, or a deeper session than the overview
  video on design controls or risk. Device-manufacturer oriented throughout. Verified loading via
  `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[21 CFR Part 820, eCFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-H/part-820)**
  — the whole of Part 820 in the government's current-text edition, so you can read 820.1, 820.3,
  820.7, and 820.10 in context rather than one section at a time. Verified loading via `curl` on
  2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA: General Principles of Software Validation](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/general-principles-software-validation)**
  — the 2002 guidance this lesson names as the one FDA points a device manufacturer to for
  validating its own device software. Read it to understand what the vendor is expected to have
  done before Release B reached you; it is written for the manufacturer, not for Lakeshore's user
  validation. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[ISPE: GAMP 5 Guide, 2nd Edition](https://ispe.org/publications/guidance-documents/gamp-5-guide-2nd-edition)**
  — the publisher's page for the industry-practice framework this lesson cites for leveraging
  supplier documentation. The guide itself is sold, so this page is a catalogue entry, not the
  text; use it to confirm what the edition is before anyone quotes it as a requirement. Verified
  loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
